item.title: Authenticated Email Hides Windows PE Inside Inline PNG IDAT Stream
item.content:encoded:
When Authentication Passes and Malware Still Walks In: A PE Hidden Inside an Inline PNG — Should Read

A fully authenticated onboarding email passed SPF, DKIM, and DMARC but hid a Windows executable inside the decompressed IDAT stream of an inline PNG image. The key lesson is that email authentication proves sender path integrity, not content safety, so defenders must inspect inline image payloads and other embedded content.

  • An onboarding email to an insurance claims examiner passed SPF, DKIM, and DMARC, with a composite authentication score of 100.
  • One inline image named image007.png was a valid, renderable PNG that contained a Windows PE header inside its decompressed IDAT stream.
  • The executable signature appeared as the bytes "MZ" at offset 696,056 inside a roughly 6.5 MB decompressed payload.
  • The article states that many secure email gateways inspect attachments more deeply than inline images, allowing this kind of embedded payload to slip through.
  • The publishable indicators include the file name image007.png, MD5 hash 4370319336a256e38dedae0c95414090, and SHA-256 hash 70fb798321c7b92e65a78a172a4429f3009216efef1c86118efd747dcceb638d.
